newsitem.title: UK: Intertanko appeals against U.S. court decision.
newsitem.headline: Intertanko appeals against U.S. court decision.

text.p: Tanker owners' association Intertanko is appealing against a U.S. court decision to uphold state regulations governing the operation of oil tankers even though they are stricter than U.S. federal laws, the association's managing director said.
"We have instructed our lawyers to appeal," said Dagfinn Lunde, managing director of the International Association of Independent tanker owners (Intertanko.)

"The international shipping community must know whether the United States departments of State and Transportation, throught the U.S. Coast Guard, can enter into binding agreements at the International Maritime Organisation and other international fora.
"If not, the leadership role of the United States in international marine and environmental fora is over."
A U.S. district court's decision in November upheld Washington state anti-pollution regulations which were imposed in the wake of the 1989 Exxon Valdez oil spill.
The decision asserted that the state regulations superseded federal laws governing marine trafic.

The state regulations require tanker operators to file oil spill prevention plans beyond what is required by federal law. Tankers operating in Washington state waters must also be equipped with an emergency towing system.

"Because we strongly believe that the safest, most effective regulatory regime is a uniform regulatory regime, we will continue to defend federal and international programmes against erosion by local governments," Lunde said. "This appeal is part of that process.
"Unles we have international regulation it is very hard to run shipping in the long run."
